summary: I found no blocker or major defect in FP-0008. I compared src/html/tokenizer.zig against the frozen whatwg/html efc54f7b source, using the local copy out/whatwg-html-source-efc54f7b…, whose SHA-256 raw/html-standard-pin.log records. I read the tokenization introduction and its definitions, the data, tag open, end tag open, and tag name states, the before attribute name state through the bogus comment, markup declaration open, and comment start states, the after DOCTYPE name and public-keyword states, the bogus DOCTYPE state, the CDATA states, the five processing instruction states, every character reference state, the numeric replacement table, the §13.2.3.5 preprocessing text, and part of the §13.2.2 table in order. For the other comment and DOCTYPE states I checked the code against the standard's well-known text, not against the frozen file. Every branch I checked follows the text. That covers EOF behavior, which characters are reconsumed, force-quirks handling, duplicate-attribute removal with the 'current attribute' kept, the historical attribute rule, saturating numeric accumulation, and the 27-row override table with the commented-out 0x0D/0x81/0x8D/0x8F/0x90/0x9D rows. I hand-traced many frozen cases (A5, A12b, A49, R1–R7, S1, S5, N6, P8, P11, P14, P20, B2, B3), and each matches. Chunk independence works as follows. consume() holds a CR or a leading surrogate at the end of the available input. Lookahead states peek raw units without consuming. release() copies only undecided units into carry. The harness overwrites each chunk with 0xAAAA after need_input. The mutation control (.more => {} in the CR branch) was applied to the committed tokenizer: blob 7ee21c8, which the GitHub contents API confirms for 9fe40c4. It failed case 13 on P1 with partition [0,2) [2,8) and 1-minimal input \r\n. The entity matcher is allocation-free and correct for a sorted table. Case 3 pins the committed table to a std.json parse of the embedded entities.json, and the regenerate run produced no diff. The lab decode and tokenize stages, the outcome precedence, and FP-0007 case 2/case 25 match the contract. I confirmed FP-0007 cases 4 and 7 are textually unchanged against parent 43edcec. Commit 9fe40c4 touches only src, tests, build.zig, and the FP-0008 evidence. Commit 00f85bc adds evidence and engineering/state.json, which stays at 'implemented' with review null. Neither commit changes a protected path. No shell code is involved. integration-binding.log records HEAD 9fe40c4 and an empty status, including ignored files, before and after the gates. The fresh-cache Zig run passed 218/218 tests, and the controller tests passed 188/188 under both Node and Bun. The remaining findings are minor or notes: case 16 uses a different chunk split than the frozen case, and the evidence has small inaccuracies and claims without a recorded command. I accept the integrator's acceptance of the extra network reads. The contract requires standard_last_updated from the live multipage page, so its 'only items 2 and 3' rule contradicted itself. The other two reads were read-only, public, and recorded, and they were used to resolve the LICENSE-commit contradiction that amendment 1 later fixed.

criteria.criterion: Exact case 16 as frozen (two chunks `<![CDA` and `TA[x]]>`).
criteria.evidence: tokenizer_test.zig:823 feeds input[0..7] (`<![CDAT`) and input[7..]. Line 837 uses boundary 7 for the flag-false A5 check. The frozen split is at offset 6.

findings.issue: Case 16 splits `<![CDATA[x]]>` at offset 7 (`<![CDAT` | `A[x]]>`), but the frozen case says the chunks are `<![CDA` and `TA[x]]>`, which is offset 6. The flag-false comparison at line 837 also uses {7}. The behavior class is the same (a stall inside the `[CDATA[` lookahead), but this is not the frozen exact case. With the flag true, no other test splits at 6.
findings.recommendation: Use input[0..6] and input[6..], and boundary {6}, to match the frozen case. Alternatively, test both 6 and 7.

findings.issue: The stop-rule observation says the 84 <h5> headings equal the frozen list and that the §13.2.2 table has 52 codes in frozen order. No recorded command produced this. The contract's integrator decision makes the same unrecorded count. I checked the PI/CDATA/character-reference section order and part of the error table by hand, and they agree, but the claim has no raw output behind it.
findings.recommendation: Record a command, such as an extraction of <h5><dfn> headings and parse-error-* dfns from out/whatwg-html-source-efc54f7b…, under raw/ and cite it.

findings.issue: The tests-before baseline was recorded at 10:45, after the entity fetch at 10:23 and after implementation, from a git-archived base. Run 1 fails only because the files do not compile. Run 2 shows only the case 26 lab steps failing. No FP-0008 tokenizer unit case is observed failing at the base, so the 'failing test first' step of AGENTS.md is shown only weakly.
findings.recommendation: State explicitly that the baseline is post hoc. In later tasks, record the failing run before implementing.

findings.issue: The frozen authority rule permits network access only for evidence items 2 and 3. The worker also fetched the multipage index, ran git ls-remote, and downloaded a comparison LICENSE. The integrator accepted these after the fact (README.md:191). The multipage fetch was needed to satisfy the contract's own standard_last_updated requirement, so the contract contradicted itself. All three reads were recorded, read-only, and public. I judge the acceptance sound, but the authority text was never amended.
findings.recommendation: Record a contract amendment, or a note in the authority section, that names the permitted reads. In future contracts, include every network read the contract itself requires.

findings.issue: The Records table lists `raw/owner-answers.log`. The file is engineering/evidence/FP-0008/owner-answers.log, not under raw/.

The generated table (BSD-3-Clause for portions in source code) names its generator and input, but not the WHATWG copyright or entities.LICENSE. The notice sits in the same directory, and entities.zig refers to it, so this is defensible for source distribution. A binary release would still need the notice reproduced, under BSD-3 clause 2.
findings.recommendation: Have entities_gen.zig emit a header line that names the WHATWG copyright and src/html/entities.LICENSE. Track binary-notice reproduction for the release task.

findings.issue: The regeneration (11:00:41) ran after the final binding check (11:00:36) and writes into src. Only `git diff` of the table file was recorded afterward, not a full source-root status.
findings.recommendation: Run the regeneration inside the binding window, or repeat the status check after it.

findings.issue: The consumeMatched doc comment says the matched characters are 'ASCII letters'. The function also consumes '-', '[', digits, and ';', which are equally free of preprocessing errors.
findings.recommendation: Reword it, for example: 'ASCII characters that a lookahead matched, which preprocessing never reports'.
